blocks.content: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions by adding a new Part IX and the 11th Schedule to the Constitution of India.

items: Article 243D mandates a minimum of 1/3rd reservation for women in Panchayats at all three levels.
Elections to local bodies must be conducted within 6 months if a Panchayat or Municipality is dissolved before its 5-year tenure.
The 11th Schedule contains 29 functional matters for Panchayats, whereas the 12th Schedule contains 18 functional matters for Municipalities.
State Election Commissioners are appointed by the Governor but can only be removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of a High Court.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 73rd Amendment Act of 1992 granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions by inserting Part IX and the 11th Schedule into the Constitution.
The 74th Amendment Act of 1992 accorded constitutional status to urban local bodies (Municipalities) by introducing Part IX-A and the 12th Schedule.
Constitutional status transferred local self-governance from discretionary state policy (Directive Principles) to an enforceable statutory constitutional framework.
The amendments created permanent statutory bodies: the State Election Commission for conducting local elections and the State Finance Commission for financial allocation.
A mandatory 33% (one-third) reservation of seats was instituted for women across all tiers of local bodies.
